items.answer: Arunima Sinha’s Seven Summits achievement is significant, making her the first woman amputee to conquer the highest peaks on every continent. items.stem: Describe Arunima’s preparation and challenges in climbing Mount Everest.
items.answer: Arunima prepared for Everest with 18 months of intense training at the Nehru Institute of Mountaineering under Bachendri Pal. Challenges included adapting to her prosthetic leg for balance and endurance, plus extreme weather and physical strain during the 52-day climb. Despite widespread doubt, her mental strength and training pushed her through. On May 21, 2013, she summited, planting the Indian flag and a Swami Vivekananda photo, marking a historic triumph.

items.stem: What is the moral of the story, and how does Arunima’s journey illustrate it?
items.answer: The moral is that courage, hard work, and self-belief overcome any challenge. Arunima’s journey vividly illustrates this: she transformed the tragedy of losing her leg into an extraordinary quest. Instead of despairing, she set her sights on Everest, trained intensely, and summitted in 2013 as the first Indian woman amputee. items.stem: Arunima showed great courage after her accident. Imagine you are Arunima preparing for Everest. What one internal fear would you tackle first?
items.answer: If I were Arunima, the first internal fear I’d tackle would be the fear of falling again. My accident on the train involved a fall, and climbing a mountain, especially with a prosthetic leg, involves great heights and risks. I would tell myself that every step is a new victory, focusing on control and belief in my training, not past trauma.

items.stem: Arunima believes “Failure is when we don’t have goals worthy enough.” How does this idea change how we usually think about failing at something?
items.answer: This idea changes how we think about failure by shifting the focus from not achieving a task to not having a meaningful goal in the first place. It suggests true failure isn’t falling short after trying, but lacking ambition or purpose. It teaches us to aim high and NODIA

items.stem: Arunima trained for 18 months for mountaineering. If you want to achieve a big goal, what one challenge would long training cause, and how would you stay motivated?
items.answer: Long training for a big goal would cause the challenge of feeling exhausted and sometimes losing motivation over time. I would overcome this by setting small, achievable steps for each day, celebrating tiny victories. I would also regularly visualize achieving my main goal, like Arunima visualizing Everest, to keep my spirit high and remind myself of the final reward.

items.stem: Arunima states, “Failure is not when we fall short of achieving our goals. It is when we don’t have goals worthy enough”. How can this message apply to a student who fails a test?
items.answer: This message tells a student that failing a test isn’t the real failure if they tried their best and had a worthy goal of learning. Instead of being discouraged, they should reflect on whether their goal for the test was strong enough. It encourages them to aim high next time, to learn from mistakes, and to always have meaningful learning goals, which is what truly matters, not just the score.

items.stem: Bachendri Pal said Arunima had “conquered the Everest within you.” Create a short conversation (two lines each) where Arunima explains this idea to a friend.
items.answer: Arunima: “Bachendri Ma’am said I won my Everest inside first.” Friend: “What does ‘Everest inside’ mean?” Arunima: “It’s about beating your biggest fears and doubts, even harder than climbing a real mountain.” Friend: “So, it’s about winning in your mind?” Extract Based Questions

items.stem: Explain how the National War Memorial and Museum app will be helpful in spreading awareness about war heroes.
items.answer: The youth of the nation and the future generations need to know about the soldiers who sacrificed their lives and their own youth to protect the country and give them the freedom that they enjoy today. It is important for them to know about each soldier, for they were bravehearts, not a number lost in the records forgotten. The National War Memorial and Museum app will spread awareness about each precious life that contributed to the freedom, sovereignty and integrity of the present.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Why is it our duty to pay homage to our brave soldiers?
items.answer: Our brave soldiers gave up their lives and youth to dedicatedly protect us and our country. They show immense selflessness, valour and inspiring endurance to such a patriotic motive. Whatever luxuries and rights we have now, it is all due to them and their fierce determination to keep us safe. They deserve gratitude and respect for their sacrifice and service. Therefore, it is our duty to pay homage to our brave soldiers.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What is the main idea of this text? How does it justify the title, ‘A Homage to our Brave Soldiers’?
items.answer: The main idea of this text is that the brave soldiers of the country should be appreciated more for their sacrifice and service. It justifies the title ‘A Homage to our Brave Soldiers’ by talking about the different ways the country and educational institutions pay homage to the soldiers who fought in the wars and protected us. For instance, it sheds light on the National War Memorial, Museum app, websites that offer insight to different soldiers, and the different awards given for the soldiers’ gallantry, Param Vir Chakra, and Maha Vir Chakra. Moreover, in the educational institutions, we see that educational trips to different war memorials are often organised for the students and competitions like collage making incur a sense of curiosity in the students which encourages them to know more about our courageous soldiers. Therefore, the text is about giving homage to soldiers and spreading awareness about their sacrifice and service.

From the 4 chakras to the row of trees planted for each soldier, every detail reminded the students of the sacrifice and service shown by each brave soldier. items.answer: Each tree represents many soldiers guarding territorial integrity. Short Answer Type Questions

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What is the meaning of “homage” as explained at the beginning of the chapter, and what is its purpose?
items.answer: Homage means “something that is said or done to show respect publicly for someone”. Its purpose is to publicly honor individuals, such as brave soldiers, for their contributions and sacrifices.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What is the National War Memorial, and what does it honour?
items.answer: The National War Memorial is a monument in New Delhi honoring Indian soldiers who sacrificed their lives in various armed conflicts since independence. It features over 26,000 names inscribed on walls and an eternal flame, symbolizing the nation’s gratitude and the immortal spirit of the fallen heroes.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: When was the National War Memorial inaugurated, and what was its location in relation to a well-known landmark?
items.answer: The National War Memorial was inaugurated in February 2019 by India’s Prime Minister. It is located “near the iconic India Gate”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What is the significance of each “tablet” at the National War Memorial, and what information does it bear?
items.answer: Each tablet is important because it “bears the names of soldiers who fought for India and made the supreme sacrifice in different wars from 1947 till date”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Name some of the specific historical conflicts for which fallen soldiers are commemorated at the Memorial.
items.answer: Fallen soldiers are commemorated for various conflicts, including the Indo-China conflict of 1962, the Indo-Pak Wars in 1965 & 1971, and the Kargil War in 1999.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What is the Param Vir Chakra, and who was the first brave soldier to be awarded this prestigious medal?
items.answer: The Param Vir Chakra (PVC) is “India’s highest wartime gallantry medal”. Major Somnath Sharma was “posthumously awarded India’s first PVC”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What does the Amar Jawan Jyoti at the Memorial symbolize, and how is it maintained?
items.answer: The Amar Jawan Jyoti symbolizes “the immortality of the spirit of fallen soldiers”. It NODIA

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: You can see the obelisk surrounded by wreaths that have been placed as a mark of respect. The lighting design is planned in such a way that it transforms the monument’s landscape as sunlight changes from dawn to dusk. It truly is a majestic site that filled me with pride for our nation. I was also overwhelmed by the interminable flame as a metaphor for eternal stories of courage and valour. Our teacher also explained the significance of the Chakras to us. I found it interesting and hence I am sharing with you. (i) What does the “interminable flame” serve as a metaphor for? (a) The changing sunlight (b) The wreaths placed on the monument (c) The pride for the nation (d) Eternal stories of courage and valour (ii) Wreaths have been placed around the obelisk as a mark of ______. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The monument’s lighting is static and does not change throughout the day. (iv) How did the majestic site make the writer feel?
items.answer: (i) (d) Eternal stories of courage and valour (ii) respect (iii) False (The extract states that the lighting design “transforms the monument’s landscape as sunlight changes from dawn to dusk”) (iv) It “filled me with pride for our nation”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: The National War Memorial consists of four concentric circles, which are known as Amar Chakra, Veerta Chakra, Tyag Chakra, and Raksha Chakra around a 15-metre-tall central obelisk with the eternal flame—the Amar Jawan Jyoti. It also houses bronze and stone murals and graphic panels. Isn’t it amazing! The innermost circle represents the Amar Chakra, also known as the ‘Circle of Immortality’. This has the Obelisk with Eternal Flame. The Amar Jawan Jyoti flame symbolises the immortality of the spirit of fallen soldiers with the assurance that the nation will never forget their sacrifice. (i) What is the innermost circle of the National War Memorial called? (a) Veerta Chakra (b) Tyag Chakra (c) Amar Chakra (d) Raksha Chakra (ii) The Amar Jawan Jyoti flame is a symbol of the ______ of the spirit of fallen soldiers. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The National War Memorial consists only of the four circles and the central obelisk. (iv) What does the Amar Jawan Jyoti flame assure the nation?
items.answer: (i) (c) Amar Chakra (ii) immortality (iii) False (The extract states, “It also houses bronze and stone murals and graphic panels”.) (iv) It gives the assurance “that the nation will never forget their sacrifice”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: How does Soumya’s visit to the National War Memorial deepen her understanding of soldiers’ sacrifices?
items.answer: Soumya’s visit to the National War Memorial deepens her understanding of soldiers’ sacrifices by honoring over 26,000 fallen heroes from various wars. Learning names on 29,000 tablets and experiencing features like the eternal flame (Amar Chakra) and sacrifice walls (Tyag Chakra) evokes pride and emotion. Inspired by heroes like Lance Naik Albert Ekka, she vows to serve the nation, reinforcing the lesson: honor and remember those who gave their lives for freedom.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What are the symbolic features of the National War Memorial, and how do they contribute to its message?
items.answer: The National War Memorial’s symbolic features powerfully convey sacrifice. The Amar Chakra’s eternal flame signifies immortal spirits. Veerta Chakra’s bronze murals depict heroic battles. Tyag Chakra’s Chakravyuh- shaped walls list over 26,000 fallen soldiers’ names. Raksha Chakra’s trees represent protectors. These symbols, with wreaths and lights, create a solemn atmosphere, instilling pride and gratitude for India’s freedom fighters, emphasizing remembrance and appreciation for their bravery.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: How does the story of Lance Naik Albert Ekka inspire Soumya, and why is it significant to the lesson?
items.answer: Lance Naik Albert Ekka’s story inspires Soumya through his immense bravery and selflessness in the 1971 war, for which he received the Param Vir Chakra. His continued fight despite severe injuries deeply moves her, sparking a desire to serve the nation. This is significant as it shows how learning about heroes cultivates patriotism and purpose in youth, fostering emotional connection to sacrifice and inspiring respect for those who protect India’s freedom.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: How does Ananda’s response to Soumya’s letter reflect his feelings about soldiers and his own aspirations?
items.answer: Ananda’s reply reflects deep respect for soldiers and strong aspirations for the Armed Forces. Soumya’s memorial description moves him, linking to his own war memorial visit and the poem Pushp ki Abhilasha. He’s inspired by heroes like Captain Anuj Nayyar and plans a school collage and uses the app. His letter, filled with gratitude and patriotism, solidifies his dream of serving the nation, embodying the lesson’s call to honor heroes.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What lessons about gratitude and courage can we learn from the letter exchange between Soumya and Ananda?
items.answer: Soumya and Ananda’s letters teach profound lessons on gratitude and courage. Soumya’s memorial visit reveals sacrifices of 26,000+ soldiers, inspiring her by heroes like Albert Ekka. Ananda’s response, recalling his own memorial visit and Pushp ki Abhilasha, shows deep appreciation. Both express desires to serve, demonstrating that remembering soldiers’ bravery fosters purpose and encourages us to live with courage, honoring those who secured our nation’s freedom.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: How does Soumya describe the National War Memorial and its symbolic sections?
items.answer: Soumya describes the National War Memorial as honoring 26,000+ soldiers from wars like 1962, 1965, 1971, and 1999. It features four symbolic sections: Amar Chakra (eternal flame), Veerta Chakra (bronze murals of battles), Tyag Chakra (walls with names), and Raksha Chakra (trees symbolizing protectors). She notes the wreaths, changing lights, and the mix of pride and sadness, emphasizing its powerful tribute to soldiers’ sacrifices. NODIA

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Explain how Ananda’s response shows his inspiration and gratitude for soldiers.
items.answer: Ananda’s response shows deep inspiration and gratitude, praising Soumya’s memorial description as a tribute to soldiers’ sacrifices. He’s moved by heroes like Captain Anuj Nayyar, empathizing with his mother’s pride and pain, which fuels his dream of joining the Armed Forces. His war memorial visit and reference to Pushp ki Abhilasha reflect emotional connection. Planning a school collage and using the memorial app further demonstrate his commitment to honoring their legacy.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What is the moral of the lesson, and how do Soumya and Ananda’s actions reflect it?
items.answer: The moral is to honor soldiers’ sacrifices and live respectfully. Soumya reflects this by visiting the National War Memorial, learning about heroes like Albert Ekka, and aspiring to serve. Ananda embodies it by expressing gratitude for soldiers’ sacrifices, inspired by Captain Anuj Nayyar, and planning a school collage. Their actions—visiting memorials, sharing stories, and aspiring to serve— demonstrate commitment to remembering those who secured India’s freedom.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Discuss how the lesson uses the letters to teach about respecting soldiers’ sacrifices.
items.answer: The letters teach respect for soldiers’ sacrifices by blending personal reflection, vivid descriptions, and inspiring stories. Soumya’s letter details the National War Memorial and heroes like Albert Ekka, evoking awe and gratitude. Her desire to serve models respect. Ananda’s response deepens this, expressing gratitude for Captain Anuj Nayyar and reflecting on broader sacrifice. Through their personal exchanges and shared commitment to honoring heroes, the narrative encourages readers to learn, remember, and live purposefully. Competency Based Questions

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Soumya visited the National War Memorial and felt deep pride. Imagine you are visiting this memorial. What one part would make you feel most proud, and why?
items.answer: If I visited the National War Memorial, the Amar Jawan Jyoti, the “immortal flame”, would make me most proud. It constantly burns to honor soldiers who died for India. This never-ending light symbolizes their bravery and sacrifice, showing that our nation will never forget their courage and what they gave for our freedom.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: The National War Memorial has names of over 26,000 fallen soldiers. Write a short paragraph about why it’s important for a nation to remember its heroes like this.
items.answer: It’s important for a nation to remember its heroes because their sacrifices protect our freedom and safety. Seeing their names reminds us of the great cost of peace. Remembering them teaches future generations about courage, patriotism, and the value of serving the country. This helps us appreciate our peaceful lives and honors those who gave everything.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Lance Naik Albert Ekka, despite being wounded, kept fighting bravely. Imagine you are in a team game. How would his bravery inspire you to keep trying even if your team is losing badly?
items.answer: If my team was losing badly, Lance Naik Albert Ekka’s bravery would inspire me to never give up. He fought even when seriously wounded, showing immense dedication. I would remember his courage and continue to play my best, even if we were losing badly. I would encourage my teammates, just as he inspired his comrades, to keep fighting until the very end. items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Soumya cried when learning about the “devastation and loss of life caused by wars.” If you could write one message on a peace poster, what would it say to prevent future wars?
items.answer: If I could write one message on a peace poster, it would say: “Understand Each Other, Not Fight Each Other: Choose Kindness.” This message would remind people that differences can be solved by talking and listening, rather than through conflict. It would encourage empathy and peaceful solutions to avoid the sadness and loss that wars bring.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Imagine you are organizing a tribute event at your school. Describe the activities you would include and why.
items.answer: If I were organizing a special event at my school to honor brave people, I would first ask my friends to help me plan it. We would begin by having everyone stand quietly for a minute to show respect. Next, some students would read short stories or poems about brave people from our town, like kind police officers or doctors who help sick people. We would also draw pictures or write thank-you notes and put them up in the school hallway for everyone to see. At the end, we would plant some trees in our school garden. Each tree would be for a brave act. This way, we would remember their good deeds for a long, long time. Extract Based Questions

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: Do you remember our last conversation about war and the importance of peace? We talked about how India had to struggle for its Independence from the British for many centuries. Post-independence our country has had to fight several wars to protect its borders, territorial integrity, and its people. This made me wonder, who were these brave Indian people? They fought to protect our country and sacrificed their lives so that we could lead our lives in peace. (i) According to the letter, for what reason has India fought several wars after its independence? (a) To show its power. (b) To protect its borders, integrity, and people. (c) To expand its territory. (d) To continue fighting the British. (ii) The writer mentions that India had to struggle for many centuries to gain ______ from the British. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The writer’s letter states that India has been completely at peace and has not fought any wars since independence. (iv) What question did the writer begin to wonder about regarding India’s post- independence wars?
items.answer: (i) (b) To protect its borders, integrity, and people. (ii) Independence (iii) False (The text says, “Post-independence our country has had to fight several wars...”) (iv) The writer began to wonder, “who were these brave Indian people?” who fought and sacrificed their lives for the country.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: We learnt that each brick of the memorial is called a tablet, and it bears the names of soldiers who fought for India and made the supreme sacrifice in different wars from 1947 till date, including the Indo-China conflict of 1962, the IndoPak Wars in 1965 & 1971 and the Kargil War in 1999. There are 29,000 tablets on which more than 26,000 names of fallen soldiers have been etched. It was heartening to know that our government has recognised the sacrifice of brave soldiers. Our teacher told us about the 21 bravehearts who were awarded the Param Vir Chakra (PVC), India’s highest wartime gallantry medal, for their service to the nation. (i) What is India’s highest wartime gallantry medal mentioned in the extract? (a) Vir Chakra (b) Maha Vir Chakra (c) Param Vir Chakra (d) Shaurya Chakra (ii) The names of the fallen soldiers have been ______ on the granite tablets. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The bricks of the memorial are blank and do not have any names on them. (iv) What information is borne on each tablet of the memorial?
items.answer: (i) (c) Param Vir Chakra (ii) etched (iii) False (The extract states that each tablet “bears the names of soldiers who fought for India and made the supreme sacrifice...”) (iv) Each tablet bears the name of a soldier who fought for India and made the supreme sacrifice in wars from 1947 to the present day.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: As we continued our visit around the National War Memorial, we came across another important installation called Amar Jawan Jyoti that commemorates our soldiers. The name, as you may have guessed, represents an immortal flame that is kept ablaze all through the day and night to revere the sacrifices of our soldiers. Earlier the Amar Jawan Jyoti, which also displayed a rifle and a helmet, was alighted under the arch of India Gate in January 1972 to commemorate India’s victory in the India-Pakistan War of 1971. (i) What was the original reason for lighting the Amar Jawan Jyoti at India Gate? (a) To celebrate the construction of the National War Memorial. (b) To commemorate India’s victory in the India-Pakistan War of 1971. (c) To mark India’s Independence Day. (d) To honour soldiers from the First World War. (ii) The Amar Jawan Jyoti represents an ______ flame that is kept ablaze day and night. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The Amar Jawan Jyoti was first lit at the National War Memorial. (iv) What two objects were displayed with the flame at the earlier Amar Jawan Jyoti?
items.answer: (i) (b) To commemorate India’s victory in the India-Pakistan War of 1971. (ii) immortal. (iii) False (The extract states, “Earlier the Amar Jawan Jyoti... was alighted under the arch of India Gate”) (iv) The earlier Amar Jawan Jyoti “also displayed a rifle and a helmet”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: The National War Memorial now includes Amar Jawan Jyoti in the obelisk, which is surrounded by four Chakras. During the inauguration, the Prime Minister lit a new flame to commemorate the fallen heroes. Later, the old flame at India Gate was also merged with the new flame at the National War Memorial. Here is a picture of the new Amar Jawan Jyoti if you haven’t seen it. (i) What happened to the old Amar Jawan Jyoti flame from India Gate? (a) It was extinguished. (b) It was merged with the new flame. (c) It was kept burning at India Gate. (d) It was moved to a museum. (ii) During the inauguration, the ______ lit a new flame to commemorate the fallen heroes. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The obelisk with the new Amar Jawan Jyoti stands by itself. (iv) Where is the new Amar Jawan Jyoti located within the National War Memorial?
items.answer: (i) (b) It was merged with the new flame. (ii) Prime Minister NODIA

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Describe the “Veerta Chakra,” also known as the ‘Circle of Bravery,’ within the National War Memorial.
items.answer: The Veerta Chakra is a “covered gallery that exhibits six murals crafted in bronze”. These murals “depicting valiant battle actions of our Armed Forces”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Explain the “Tyag Chakra,” or ‘Circle of Sacrifice,’ and what its circular design signifies.
items.answer: The Tyag Chakra has “circular concentric walls of honour” covered with granite tablets, inscribed with names. Its design “symbolizes the ancient war formation, which is called Chakravyuh”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What is the purpose of the “Raksha Chakra” (Circle of Protection) with its distinctive row of trees?
items.answer: The Raksha Chakra’s row of trees is “a reassurance to the citizens of the country about their safety against any threat”. Each tree represents “many soldiers who guard territorial integrity”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What is the Amar Chakra at the National War Memorial?
items.answer: The Amar Chakra, or Circle of Immortality, at the National War Memorial is home to the eternal flame, symbolising that the spirits of fallen soldiers live on. It represents the everlasting legacy of their bravery and sacrifice, creating a solemn and respectful atmosphere at the memorial.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Who is Lance Naik Albert Ekka, and why does Soumya admire him?
items.answer: Lance Naik Albert Ekka was a soldier who fought bravely in the 1971 Indo-Pak War, continuing to battle despite serious injuries until he died. Soumya admires him for his courage and selflessness, inspired by his story to serve the nation, as his gallantry earned him the Param Vir Chakra.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What does Ananda recall about his visit to a war memorial in Chandigarh?
items.answer: Ananda recalls visiting a war memorial in Chandigarh’s Bougainvillaea Garden, where people laid flowers to honour fallen soldiers. This visit reminds him of the Hindi poem Pushp ki Abhilasha by Makhanlal Chaturvedi, where a flower wishes to honour brave soldiers, deepening his respect for their sacrifices.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Who is Captain Anuj Nayyar, and how does Ananda learn about him?
items.answer: Captain Anuj Nayyar was a brave soldier in the Kargil War who was awarded the Maha Vir Chakra after his death. Ananda learns about him from an interview with Nayyar’s mother, who wrote an emotional book about her son, expressing both her pain and pride in remembering him.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What profound personal impact did the visit to the National War Memorial have on the narrator, Soumya?
items.answer: Soumya stated the visit “filled me with pride for our nation” and “motivated me to live a life worthy of the sacrifices of our heroes”. It was an “emotive experience”. Long Answer Type Questions

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Describe the story of one war hero mentioned in Soumya’s letter and its impact on her.
items.answer: Soumya is deeply inspired by Lance Naik Albert Ekka, a 1971 Indo-Pak War hero awarded the Param Vir Chakra. Despite severe injuries, Ekka fought with immense courage until his death. His bravery and selflessness profoundly move Soumya, igniting a strong desire to serve the nation. His sacrifice highlights soldiers’ immense courage, strengthening her admiration and motivating her to honor their legacy through her actions and aspirations for national contribution. items.answer: (i) (b) solemn and a reminder of achievement. (ii) bond. (iii) False (The extract states, “We spent the whole day, from morning to evening, at the National War Memorial”.) (iv) The surrounding areas were “marked by majestic lawns and grand buildings of Kartavyapath”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: On 28 June 1999, Major Padmapani Acharya as a Company Commander, was assigned the formidable task of capturing an enemy position which was heavily fortified, strongly held and covered with mines and sweeping machine gun and artillery fire. Success of the battalion and brigade operation hinged on the early capture of this position. However, the company attack almost faltered at the very beginning when the enemy’s artillery fire came down squarely on the leading platoon, inflicting large number of casualties. (i) Why was the early capture of the enemy position considered critical? (a) Because it had valuable resources. (b) Because the success of the battalion and brigade operation depended on it. (c) Because it was the last objective of the war. (d) Because it was an easy target to begin with. (ii) The task was formidable because the enemy position was heavily fortified and covered with mines, machine gun, and ______ fire. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The attack on the enemy position was easy and successful from the very beginning. (iv) What caused the company’s attack to nearly fail at the start?
items.answer: (i) (b) Because the success of the battalion and brigade operation depended on it. (ii) artillery (iii) False (The extract states, “the company attack almost faltered at the very beginning when the enemy’s artillery fire came down squarely on the leading platoon, inflicting large number of casualties”.) (iv) The attack nearly failed because “the enemy’s artillery fire came down squarely on the leading platoon, inflicting large number of casualties”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: I was happy to hear that you got an opportunity to visit the National War Memorial. I have heard a lot about it. Some people might see a war memorial as just a monument, statue, an edifice to celebrate our war heroes or victory and commemorate those who lost their lives or got injured in the war. In my view, it is also an expression of deep gratitude for the supreme sacrifice made by our brave soldiers defending the sovereignty and integrity of the country. I feel motivated and I am seriously thinking of joining the Armed Forces to serve my motherland. (i) In the writer’s personal view, a war memorial is an expression of what? (a) A celebration of victory (b) A monument to the injured (c) Deep gratitude for soldiers’ sacrifice (d) A place to remember war heroes (ii) The writer feels motivated and is seriously thinking of joining the ______ to serve the motherland. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The writer had no knowledge of the National War Memorial before receiving the letter. (iv) According to the writer, what were the soldiers defending when they made their supreme sacrifice?
items.answer: (i) (c) Deep gratitude for soldiers’ sacrifice (ii) Armed Forces (iii) False (The writer states, “I have heard a lot about it”.) (iv) They were “defending the sovereignty and integrity of the country”.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: Very recently, I read in the newspaper that Captain Anuj Nayyar, MVC, an Indian Army officer of the 17 Jat regiment was posthumously awarded the Maha Vir Chakra, India’s second highest gallantry award, for exemplary valour during the Kargil War in 1999. items.answer: (i) (c) The Kargil War in 1999 (ii) Tiger (iii) False (The extract states he was “posthumously awarded” the Maha Vir Chakra, which means he received it after his death.) (iv) His mother, Meena Nayyar, wrote the memoir about him.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: Next week, I am going to share this idea with my classmates and my teacher. I think it would be great to create a collage capturing the lives and stories of people that can inspire us each day. I know that we can email each other. I really like to receive letters from you, not just because of the ideas that you share but also because the envelope of your letters often comes with beautiful stamps, which make me happy. I don’t know if I ever shared it before, but collecting stamps is one of my favourite hobbies. I’ve been doing it for years. But I learnt recently that the act of collecting stamps is called ‘philately’. This time I received a stamp that celebrates India’s independence, a theme related to your letter. (i) What hobby does the writer reveal in this part of the letter? (a) Creating collages (b) Writing letters (c) Collecting stamps (d) Studying history (ii) The writer recently learned that the act of collecting stamps is called ‘______’. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The writer likes receiving letters only for the ideas shared in them. (iv) What theme did the stamp that the writer received celebrate?
items.answer: (i) (c) Collecting stamps (ii) philately (iii) False (The writer states, “I really like to receive letters from you, not just because of the ideas that you share but also because the envelope of your letters often comes with beautiful stamps”.) (iv) The stamp “celebrates India’s independence”.  NODIA

The chimes’ gentle sound also mirrors the poet’s prayer for soldiers’ safety, signifying lasting honor and the deep appreciation soldiers inspire.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Why does the poet compare soldiers to yogis in the second stanza, and how does this enhance the poem’s message?
items.answer: The poet compares soldiers to yogis in the second stanza to highlight their profound discipline, focus, and strength in solitude. Like yogis, soldiers maintain unwavering vigilance in harsh elements—wind, snow, heat—without complaint. This comparison elevates their duty to a spiritual mission, emphasizing their quiet dedication and resilience. It deepens reader respect and gratitude for their tireless, selfless protection of the nation.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: How does the third stanza illustrate the diverse roles of soldiers in protecting the nation?
items.answer: The third stanza illustrates soldiers’ diverse protective roles. They scale “mountains,” traverse “valleys,” brave “hot deserts,” and navigate “wet marshes,” signifying their presence across varied terrains. “Guarding the seas and skies” further emphasizes their comprehensive protection—on land, air, and water. By stating they give the “prime of their youth,” the stanza underscores their immense sacrifice across all these challenging environments for national safety.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What role does the imagery in the poem play in expressing gratitude for soldiers’ service?
items.answer: The poem’s imagery profoundly expresses gratitude for soldiers’ service. Stanza 1 evokes thankfulness, picturing sleepless “Defenders.” Stanza 2’s “yogis” enduring wind, snow, and heat instills respect for their quiet strength. Stanza 3’s expansive landscapes— mountains, deserts, seas, skies—show their vast efforts. The final stanza’s “wind chimes” symbolize national remembrance and prayer, consolidating profound appreciation for their unwavering courage and sacrifice.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What lessons about gratitude and respect can we learn from the poem’s tribute to soldiers?
items.answer: The poem teaches profound gratitude and respect for soldiers. It highlights their sleepless vigilance, endurance of harsh weather (snow, heat), and solitary service in remote areas. Soldiers’ diverse roles—in mountains, deserts, seas, sky—and sacrificing their “prime of youth” for national safety are emphasized. The “wind chimes” of bravery and the concluding prayer reinforce the moral: honor soldiers’ sacrifices, remember their courage, and live respectfully.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What is the moral of the poem, and how does the poet’s tone reflect it?
items.answer: The moral of the poem is to respect and be thankful for soldiers’ sacrifices, praying for their safety. The poet’s tone, filled with admiration and emotion, reflects this. Calling them “great sons” who protect while others sleep (stanzas 1-2), and detailing their work across diverse terrains (stanza 3), showcases deep respect. The concluding prayer, “We pray for you brave men!!”, expresses heartfelt care, urging gratitude for their selfless service.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Discuss how the poem inspires gratitude and respect for soldiers’ dedication.
items.answer: The poem inspires gratitude and respect by vividly portraying soldiers’ sacrifices. Stanza 1’s “Defenders of borders,” forsaking sleep, highlights their selflessness. Stanza 2 describes their endurance against “wind, snow, or heat,” like disciplined “yogis,” fostering admiration for their resilience. Stanza 3 details their service across mountains, deserts, seas, and skies, sacrificing their youth. The “wind chimes” in the final stanza symbolize national homage, culminating in a heartfelt prayer, collectively inspiring profound thankfulness. Competency Based Questions

items.stem: What you have learnt from her
items.answer: Good morning, respected teachers and my dear classmates! Our group is excited to present on Kalpana Chawla, a truly brave woman who inspires us. Born in Karnal, Haryana, India, she was curious about airplanes from childhood and dreamt of going to space one day. Kalpana was very dedicated to her studies, earning an engineering degree in India. She pursued higher studies in the U.S. for her Master’s and Ph.D., later becoming a flight instructor. She was then selected by NASA for astronaut training. Kalpana Chawla made history in 1997 as the first Indian-origin woman in space, flying on Space Shuttle Columbia (STS-87). She had a second mission in 2003 (STS-107), spending many days conducting experiments in space. Her biggest contribution was inspiring millions globally, especially girls, to pursue dreams in science and space. She proved that with hard work and courage, anything is possible, expanding human knowledge through her space research. From Kalpana Chawla, we learned never to give up on our dreams, no matter how big. Her life teaches us the importance of hard work, dedication, curiosity, and always aiming for the stars. Thank you!

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Discuss how Rani Abbakka’s story inspires others to stand up for freedom.
items.answer: Rani Abbakka’s story is truly inspiring, highlighting her bravery and strategic leadership in defending her kingdom’s independence. She refused to submit to Portuguese demands, rallying local rajas and forging alliances to strengthen her kingdom’s position. Her resilience in the four-day battle and subsequent attack on the Portuguese fort left a lasting legacy. Her actions not only ensured Ullal’s freedom but also motivated other rulers to resist foreign domination, making her a powerful symbol of courage and determination.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: What is the moral of the story, and how does Rani Abbakka’s leadership reflect it?
items.answer: The moral is that courage and determination lead to victory and inspire independence. Rani Abbakka exemplifies this by fearlessly refusing Portuguese demands, rallying local rajas, and building alliances. Her leadership during the four-day battle and fort attack demonstrated unwavering resolve for freedom. Her actions empowered her people and other rulers, embodying the moral of standing firm for justice and independence against powerful opponents.

items.answer: Rani Abbakka showed determination by defiantly refusing Portuguese tribute and declaring Ullal independent. She stood firm despite her husband’s objections and his attempts to deter her with soldiers. Abbakka further demonstrated resolve by uniting local rulers, building merchant ships, and allying with the Zamorin of Kozhikode. Her fearless leadership fighting alongside soldiers in a four-day battle and attacking the Portuguese fort showcased unwavering commitment to Ullal’s freedom. NODIA

Her leadership in uniting local rajas and allying with the Zamorin of Kozhikode, combined with her direct involvement in battle, showcases deep dedication. Her fearless spirit secured Ullal’s independence and inspired broader resistance, proving that standing up for justice, even against odds, leads to victory and freedom.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers

items.answer: Rani Abbakka faced formidable challenges: the powerful Portuguese, her husband’s opposition, and skeptical local rajas. She overcame them through determination and strategic thinking. She forged crucial alliances, like with the Zamorin of Kozhikode, and strengthened Ullal by building merchant ships. Her fearless leadership united and inspired her people, leading to victory. Her resilience, courage, and strategic planning ultimately secured her kingdom’s independence, proving obstacles can be surmounted through unity.

items.answer: Rani Abbakka’s story teaches powerful lessons in courage and leadership. Her strategic unity—rallying rajas and allying with the Zamorin—shows persuasive leadership. Leading her soldiers in battle demonstrates hands-on courage. items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: ABBAKKA: I WILL STOP PAYING TRIBUTE TO THE PORTUGUESE. I WILL NOT SELL THEM SPICES AND CLOTH EITHER. VEERA NARASIMHA: ISN’T THAT A RATHER RASH DECISION? ABBAKKA: YOU MAY BE AFRAID OF THE PORTUGUESE. BUT I REFUSE TO BE COWED BY THEM. (i) What was King Veera Narasimha’s opinion of Abbakka’s plan? (a) He thought it was a brave plan. (b) He thought it was a rash decision. (c) He wanted to join her immediately. (d) He was indifferent to her plan. (ii) In addition to stopping the tribute, Abbakka also decided not to sell the Portuguese ______ and cloth. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: Rani Abbakka was scared of the Portuguese and followed her husband’s cautious advice. (iv) What were the two actions Rani Abbakka declared she would take against the Portuguese?
items.answer: (i) (b) He thought it was a rash decision. (ii) spices (iii) False (She explicitly states, “I REFUSE TO BE COWED BY THEM.”) (iv) She declared that she would stop paying tribute to the Portuguese and would not sell them spices and cloth.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: PORTUGUESE ENVOY: “OUR GOVERNOR HAS SENT ME TO REMIND YOU THAT THE ANNUAL TRIBUTE FROM ULLAL IS LONG OVERDUE. AND...” RANI ABBAKKA: “WE ARE A SOVEREIGN COUNTRY. WE DON’T PAY TRIBUTE TO PORTUGAL. AND WE DON’T TAKE ORDERS FROM THE PORTUGUESE!” PORTUGUESE ENVOY: “YOUR MAJESTY, YOU WILL REGRET YOUR STAND.” (i) What reason does Rani Abbakka give for refusing to pay the tribute? (a) She claims Ullal is a sovereign country. (b) She states that the tribute is too expensive. (c) She says the Governor is not her king. (d) She argues that the tribute was never agreed upon. (ii) The Portuguese envoy warned the queen that she would ______ her stand. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: Rani Abbakka politely agreed to pay the tribute as soon as possible. (iv) What was the message from the Portuguese Governor that the envoy delivered?
items.answer: (i) (a) She claims Ullal is a sovereign country. (ii) regret (iii) False (She firmly stated, “WE DON’T PAY TRIBUTE TO PORTUGAL.”) (iv) The envoy’s message was a reminder that the annual tribute from Ullal was long overdue.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: NARRATOR: WHEN RIBERO BROUGHT THE NEWS OF THE FALL OF FORT MANGALORE, THE PORTUGUESE GOVERNOR OF GOA REACTED SHARPLY. GOVERNOR: WHAT! A MERE WOMAN DEFEATING THE MIGHTY PORTUGUESE! YOU HAVE MADE US THE LAUGHING-STOCK OF THE LOCAL RULERS. (i) How did the Portuguese Governor react to the news of the defeat? (a) He was calm and understanding. (b) He reacted sharply and angrily. (c) He was pleased with Ribero’s efforts. (d) He decided to surrender. (ii) The Governor felt that the defeat had made the Portuguese the ______ of the local rulers. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The Governor was proud that a woman had been able to defeat his forces. (iv) Who brought the news of the fall of Fort Mangalore to the Governor of Goa?
items.answer: (i) (b) He reacted sharply and angrily. (ii) laughing-stock (iii) False (The Governor was angry, exclaiming, “WHAT! A MERE WOMAN DEFEATING THE MIGHTY PORTUGUESE!”) (iv) The commander, Ribero, brought the news to the Governor.

items.chapter: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
items.stem: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: VEERA NARASIMHA: STOP HER! SEIZE HER!! NARRATOR: BUT SUCH WAS THE SPELL CAST BY THE BRAVE QUEEN. NOT A SOLDIER STIRRED. THEY DECIDED TO FOLLOW THEIR BRAVE LEADER. (i) What did King Veera Narasimha order his soldiers to do? (a) To follow the queen. (b) To ignore the queen. (c) To seize the queen. (d) To protect the queen. (ii) The narrator states that “NOT A SOLDIER ______” because of the spell cast by the queen. (iii) State whether the following statement is true or false: The soldiers obeyed their king’s command without hesitation. (iv) What did the soldiers decide to do after the king gave his order?
items.answer: (i) (c) To seize the queen. (ii) STIRRED (iii) False (The text states, “NOT A SOLDIER STIRRED.”) (iv) They “DECIDED TO FOLLOW THEIR BRAVE LEADER.” NODIA

items.answer: (D) A is false but R is true. Assertion A is false; the Rajas responded with “Impossible! We are no match for them”. Reason R is true and explains their refusal: they “felt they would be no match for the Portuguese army and their power”.
